meta.title: Olavo de Carvalho — Chronology
meta.subtitle: Chronology of Olavo de Carvalho (1947–2022): life and works
meta.description: An open, source-referenced chronology of Olavo de Carvalho — self-taught philosopher and polemicist, teacher of the Curso Online de Filosofia and the central intellectual reference of the Brazilian New Right; earlier a journalist, and briefly a professional astrologer.
meta.dataQualityNote: Work-in-progress dataset compiled from public sources (see references). Contested claims — above all his influence on the Bolsonaro government, the cause of his death, and the episodes of his early trajectory — are attributed to their authors, never asserted in this site's voice. Dates not verified against a primary source are flagged. Corrections against primary sources are welcome.

threads.note: These lanes are an editorial reading of a contested life, not a neutral fact: the currents are the ones he himself named as his formation — in a 2012 lecture he called it his great sin to have spent 'thirty-some years absorbing all the influences' (per the community transcriptions) — plus the public roles the record documents. Lanes are containers for dated events, never a claim that the currents weigh the same. Left out as lanes, deliberately: family life (private; it appears only where already public), the transcription corpus's internal scholarship (its own project), and the Brazilian New Right ecosystem around him (a distinct, living-persons subject).

lanes.label: Illness & the body
lanes.basis: His own repeated origin story — sick from birth, seven years bedridden — which he himself tied to his drive to understand human situations (lectures of 2010-10-09 and after), through the 2018 surgery and the final year.

lanes.label: Journalism & the press
lanes.basis: His own periodization of his livelihood (working from 14, journalism at 17 for the five-hour day; lecture of 2010-11-13) and the press-career record (obituaries; the Comunique-se profile).

lanes.label: Communist youth
lanes.basis: His own bracketing (1964 not yet militant; 'twenty years cleaning it out') and the BBC Brasil interview profile's 1966–1968.

lanes.label: Astrology & the esoteric quest
lanes.basis: His own master list of the seeker years (lecture of 2012-09-08: psychoanalyses, New Age, Rosicrucians, astrology, 'macumbas', Islamic esoterism) and Calil's account of the Escola Júpiter period.

lanes.label: Traditionalism & the tariqa
lanes.basis: Mark Sedgwick's scholarship of the Maryamiyya episode and his own tellings (met Schuon 1986, muqaddam on arrival, about a year and a half).

lanes.label: Catholic return
lanes.basis: His own dated lecture statements (Padre Paulo Ricardo named his personal confessor, 2010-10-30; confession practice into 2020) and the deathbed-sacraments account.

lanes.label: Philosophy & teaching
lanes.basis: The works record (the 1994–96 books onward, the Seminário, the 585-lecture COF) and his self-periodization: teaching since 1989, first book at 48.

lanes.label: Politics & attributed influence
lanes.basis: Press and academic characterizations — always attributed, and rejected by him in his own dated words — plus his documented 2020–21 rift statements.

facts.label: Who
facts.value: Olavo Luiz Pimentel de Carvalho — self-taught philosopher and polemicist, from 2009 teacher of the Curso Online de Filosofia (COF); earlier a journalist, and a professional astrologer around 1979–1982

facts.label: Died
facts.value: Night of 24 January 2022, in a hospital in the Richmond, Virginia area (USA), aged 74; announced by the family in the early hours of 25 January. The cause was publicly disputed — see the chronology

facts.label: Residency
facts.value: Brazilian citizen; resident in the United States (Richmond, Virginia area) from 2005 until his death; buried at St. Joseph's Cemetery, Petersburg, Virginia

facts.label: Decorations
facts.value: Medalha do Pacificador (Brazilian Army, 25 August 1999); Comendador of Romania's Ordinul naţional Pentru Merit (by decree of President Emil Constantinescu, 5 December 2000); Medalha Mérito Santos Dumont (Brazilian Air Force, 20 July 2001); Grã-Cruz of the Ordem de Rio Branco (2019 — contested, see chronology). The two Brazilian days and months are his own CV's; the Romanian date is the decree's.

facts.label: Family
facts.value: Married to Roxane Andrade de Souza; eight children and eighteen grandchildren at his death

events.title: Born in Campinas, São Paulo
events.text: Born Olavo Luiz Pimentel de Carvalho. Obituaries note he had little formal schooling and described himself as self-taught.

events.title: Brief affiliation with the Brazilian Communist Party (PCB)
events.text: A BBC Brasil profile built on an in-person interview (Fellet, December 2016) states 'Entre 1966 e 1968, militou no Partido Comunista'; the historian Gilberto Calil records a brief PCB passage in the 1960s without exact dates. The dating rests on his own recollection as relayed by the interviewer, so the flag stays. In the course he bracketed the period himself: in 1964 he was a secondary student with vague leftist sympathy, not yet a militant, and he recalled joining the party 'to stir up trouble' and spending twenty years working the influence out of himself (lectures of 2009 and 2014, per the community transcriptions).

events.title: First contributions to Folha de S.Paulo
events.text: Both Wikipedias date his first Folha de S.Paulo piece (in the Folhetim section, on The Magic Flute) to February 1977. Other sources push his journalism back earlier — Gazeta do Povo says he started at 17 at Folha da Manhã; Calil says he began writing for major newspapers in 1967. The sources do not reconcile these, and they may describe different roles. His own telling in the course: working from age 14 to ease his mother's burden, and entering journalism at 17 expressly because the legal five-hour day left time to study (lecture of 13 November 2010, among others), with the professional registry later obtained by time of service.

events.title: Co-founds the Escola Júpiter de Astrologia
events.text: Worked professionally as an astrologer c. 1979–1982, co-founding the school and its Revista de Astrologia Júpiter and collaborating on a university-extension astrology course at PUC-SP; Calil (2021) reports the school had about 140 students by 1980. He later abandoned and disavowed astrology. His own telling in the course: professionally an astrologer for about two years, with some 5,000 charts interpreted — psychiatrists sent him patients' horoscopes — and the school closing around 1980; he quit after judging the techniques unserious.

events.title: First book: A Imagem do Homem na Astrologia
events.text: The 1980 date belongs to a 38-page booklet (Ed. Júpiter), grown out of the 1979 PUC-SP astrology course. Olavo's own CV opens its 'Livros publicados' list with three 1983 titles (Speculum) — which explains Agência Brasil's 'first book, 1983': the two dates describe different things (a course booklet vs. his first books proper). The 1980 edition is attested only by book-trade listings, so the flag stays.

events.title: Enters the Traditionalist / Perennialist milieu
events.text: Per Calil (2021), around 1982 he joined an esoteric 'Tradition' group. Sedgwick's peer-reviewed history of Brazilian Traditionalism (2021) documents the arc: an interest in Traditionalism from 1977, after he was given Jacob Needleman's anthology The Sword of Gnosis; Michel Veber's 1980 lecture on Guénon at the Escola Júpiter and a further series in 1981; his own translation of Guénon's La Métaphysique orientale (A Metafísica Oriental, Escola Júpiter, 1981); an article in the New Age magazine Planeta (no. 107, August 1981) calling Veber 'my professor' — in which he also wrote that Veber had studied under Guénon's personal guidance, which Sedgwick notes was impossible, Veber having been four years old when Guénon left France in 1930; the founding of an Instituto de Estudos Tradicionais; and the first Traditionalist article to appear in a major Brazilian newspaper, 'Moralidade sem Deus?' (Jornal da Tarde, 27 February 1982). He also led followers into A Tradição, the organization of Omar Ali Shah, and broke with it after concluding its leader was a 'con-man' (Sedgwick, quoting his term) — a public dispute that reached the police. Approximate dating for the group entry itself; all characterizations are these scholars'.

events.title: Involvement with Sufi Islam (the Maryamiyya of Frithjof Schuon)
events.text: Calil (2021) states he converted to Islam in 1984, took the name Sidi Mohammad Ibrahim, and set up a tariqa of his own that dissolved within months. Sedgwick (2021) documents the sequence from the Lings correspondence: after contacting Marco Pallis, Carvalho and some of his followers corresponded with Martin Lings, who explained that 'entering Islam' was the appropriate preparation for the Maryami tariqa — which they did. Lings's letters address him as 'Sidi Muhammad' from June 1985; they were deposited at the São Paulo state court in 1990 as evidence in a case brought by a former follower, which Carvalho won. Sedgwick places him at the 1985 Traditionalist conference in Lima where Lings was present, but marks that presence as deduced rather than documented; he records that in 1986 Carvalho led a group of Brazilians to Bloomington, Indiana, where Schuon appointed him muqaddam (Sufi representative) for Brazil. Carvalho himself later said he had 'entered' Islam rather than converted, in Guénon's sense. On the exit Sedgwick is only relative — 'within a few years' he became disenchanted, telling an interviewer he had discovered that Schuon backed a rival for the leadership of the Brazilian Maryamiyya and had endorsed rumours against him — which converges with his own telling in the course: met Schuon in 1986, made muqaddam on arrival, stayed about a year and a half, provoked his own expulsion, placing the exit around 1987–88 (per the community transcriptions). He later disavowed the period's books as reflecting 'more a duty of obedience' to Schuon than his own thought.

events.title: Publishes Fronteiras da Tradição, his first book beyond astrology
events.text: Lectures from his Traditionalist teaching period — several first given at the Editora Astrociência in Rio de Janeiro — are published as Fronteiras da Tradição (São Paulo: Nova Stella, 1986), per Sedgwick (2021) his first book on a topic other than astrology. Its references are 'almost without exception' the major Traditionalist authors; it urges an orthodox religion as the exoteric frame for esoteric practice and warns against pseudo-initiatic organizations, citing A Tradição as an example. The volume also reprints the 1982 Jornal da Tarde article.

events.title: The course his CV calls the seminar's beginning
events.text: His curriculum vitae lists a course called “Introdução à Vida Intelectual”, taught from March 1987 to March 1989 at the Instituto Sto. André in Rio de Janeiro, and adds that under the name Seminário Permanente de Filosofia e Humanidades it “continues to this day” in São Paulo. That is his own claim of an unbroken teaching line, and it is the only dated origin the seminar has: no independent record of a founding has been found, and the organization entry keeps the date unverified. It sits beside rather than against the “teaching since 1989” he gives in the online course — the Rio course ends in March 1989 and the renamed seminar takes over from there, so the two self-datings mark different starting points. The sentence carrying the claim is undated, like the rest of the document: the CV's sections were revised at different times, so “to this day” dates from whenever that paragraph was last touched. Its list of internal course handouts — forty-two fascicles under the Seminário Permanente name — is the only other trace of the course in it.

events.title: Publishes A Nova Era e a Revolução Cultural
events.text: On Gramsci and Fritjof Capra (Instituto de Artes Liberais); obituaries treat it as the book that established him as a conservative polemicist.

events.title: Publishes O Jardim das Aflições
events.text: Subtitled 'de Epicuro à ressurreição de César' (Diadorim); later republished, and the source of the 2017 documentary's title.

events.title: Publishes O Imbecil Coletivo
events.text: His polemic against the Brazilian intelligentsia ('atualidades inculturais brasileiras'); Calil (2021) notes it achieved significant circulation and made him a public figure.

events.title: Publishes Aristóteles em Nova Perspectiva
events.text: His 'theory of the four discourses' reading of Aristotle (Topbooks); year and publisher rest on a single tertiary source.

events.title: Receives the Medalha do Pacificador (Brazilian Army)
events.text: His curriculum vitae dates the medal to 25 August 1999 and names the Brazilian Army Command as the conferring authority. Maria Cristina Fernandes, writing in Valor Econômico in April 2019, puts it in the same year as a lecture he gave to a military audience and attributes it to the then army minister, General Gleuber Vieira, who she reports had also written to him praising his work as “intelligent, prudent, balanced and full of good sense”. She does not name the lecture; the only military one his CV dates to 1999 is “Reparando uma injustiça pessoal” at the Clube Militar in Rio de Janeiro on 31 March. Agência Brasil's obituary career summary records the medal without a date.
events.dateNote: The year is in Agência Brasil's obituary and the circumstances are in Valor Econômico; the exact day, 25 August 1999, comes from his own CV and has not been checked against an Army bulletin.

events.title: Speaks at the 13th Fórum da Liberdade
events.text: His earliest surviving recorded appearance. The edition's theme was the Brazilian quincentenary — 'Mil anos: o Brasil em perspectiva' — and he argued that a country reflecting on five hundred years of history had collapsed the question into a quarrel about present economic policy. He named the gap a parallax, borrowing the term from photography, and applied it to the lettered class rather than to an individual. Olívio Dutra, then governor of Rio Grande do Sul, had spoken from the same platform, and Carvalho answered him by name while calling him honest. The recording does not state the edition number; it is fixed by the Forum's own list of editions.

events.title: Made a Commander of Romania's Ordinul naţional Pentru Merit
events.text: Decree 581 of 5 December 2000, signed by President Emil Constantinescu and countersigned by Prime Minister Mugur Isărescu, confers the Ordinul naţional Pentru Merit on a list of Brazilian and Romanian recipients “in recognition of the contribution made to the development of Romanian-Brazilian relations”. In the rank of Comandor, between an art collector and an honorary consul, stands “domnului Olavo de Carvalho, profesor universitar” — a description the decree supplies and that appears nowhere in his own curriculum vitae. The decree was published in Monitorul Oficial I no. 648 of 12 December 2000, and Romanian press coverage of his death cited it again in January 2022. His CV records the same decoration and the same date, and documents the Romanian connection behind it: a paper at the Latinité et Nouvel Ordre Mondial congress in Cluj-Napoca in July 1998, Bucharest radio and press interviews in late 1998, and a lecture on twentieth-century Brazilian philosophers at the Casa de América Latina in Bucharest on 8 September 1999.

events.title: Receives the Medalha Mérito Santos Dumont (Brazilian Air Force)
events.text: Recorded without a date in Agência Brasil's obituary career summary. His own curriculum vitae dates it to 20 July 2001 and names the Comando da Aeronáutica as the conferring authority.
events.dateNote: The year is in Agência Brasil's obituary; the exact day, 20 July 2001, comes from his own CV and is not independently confirmed.

events.title: Founds the website Mídia Sem Máscara
events.text: A media-criticism site against what it described as leftist bias in the Brazilian press; Calil (2021) treats it as his main ideological platform from 2002 until it went offline around 2017.
events.dateNote: The .org domain was registered 24 July 2002 and the site was serving content by 11 August, which is an independent bound on the founding year rather than a restatement of it.

events.title: Records the Curso História Essencial da Filosofia — already its fifth delivery
events.text: An eight-session history-of-philosophy course, videotaped by the publisher É Realizações, running from the pre-Socratics to the advent of Christianity. He dates it on the recordings themselves and says he has already taught it four times, the first in Rio in 1993 — so this is a fifth delivery of a course a decade old, not a new one. It is taught live and in person, in the same room as his separate Seminário de Filosofia, which he mentions meets the following day: the seminar therefore existed in Brazil three years before he emigrated. The recordings are the fullest systematic statement of his reading of the philosophers before the Curso Online de Filosofia begins in 2009, and the printed collection drawn from them runs to 2006.

events.title: Speaks at the 15th Fórum da Liberdade, on the future of democracy
events.text: On the edition's theme, 'Os desafios da democracia no século XXI'. He set out three dangers to democracy: Gramsci's hegemony and expanded state, sold under the name of organised civil society; the extension of democracy past the political and juridical domain, which he says turns it into its opposite; and a third he named himself, liberal economicism. The recording does not state the edition number, and predates the October presidential election — the floor questions refer to that year's candidates as still running.

events.title: Debates Eduardo Bueno on culture and development at the 17th Fórum da Liberdade
events.text: The moderator names the edition from the stage. Bueno gave the sixteenth century; Carvalho gave the present, arguing that the Brazilian constitutional definition of culture — whatever bears witness to a mode of existence — puts culture at the antipodes of cultivation and cult, and that no burst of philosophical creativity in history has followed an economic boom. He named Mário Ferreira dos Santos as a philosopher of world rank whom Brazil had left out of print.

events.title: Moves to the United States
events.text: Settled in the Richmond, Virginia area, where he lived until his death. The year is given consistently across obituaries and profiles — all of them secondary — and he confirms it himself on air: answering a caller on 8 October 2007 who had just left Brazil, he says he has been here two years, which puts the move in the second half of 2005 and is the only first-person dating of it found so far. In the same answer he says his first visit to the United States was in 1986, when he was already a grown man, married and the father of several children — the year the traditionalist material places him at Bloomington.

events.title: Shares a platform with Oded Grajew at the 18th Fórum da Liberdade
events.text: Announced from the stage as the eighteenth edition, on 'A cultura do trabalho', with the Sri Lankan-Australian jurist Suri Ratnapala and Oded Grajew, a founder of the World Social Forum, whose Porto Alegre meetings this Forum was founded against. Grajew left before Carvalho's turn. Carvalho described a seventy-year cycle of state intervention in labour relations, then reframed the debate as an asymmetry of forces rather than a contest of programmes — naming the industrialist Jorge Gerdau and a handful of businessmen on one side and, on the other, the FARC, the Foro de São Paulo, the European Union, the United Nations and the great American foundations. Months later he emigrated.

events.title: First dated lecture to a Washington audience, at the Atlas Foundation
events.text: Four months after he settled in Virginia, his curriculum vitae records a talk titled “Brazilian left: from victory to defeat to victory again” at the Atlas Foundation for Economic Studies in Arlington, Virginia. His English-language résumé gives the same date to a talk at the “Atlas Economic Research Foundation” in Washington D.C., and adds a second talk eight days later at Georgetown University's Center for Latin American Studies on 23 September 2005 that the Portuguese CV omits altogether. Both documents are his own; no programme, report or recording of either occasion has been found.

events.dateNote: The conference is externally dated and located; his appearance on its programme rests on his own CV, whose English counterpart dates the same talk a year later.
events.title: The São Paulo Forum thesis, delivered to the Intelligence Summit
events.text: His curriculum vitae records a talk titled “Neocommunist rise: The São Paulo Forum and the Strategical Unity of the Latin-American Left” at the Intelligence Summit 2006 in Arlington, Virginia, on 19 February 2006 — the earliest dated presentation of his São Paulo Forum thesis to a United States audience that any of his own documents record. The occasion itself is independently documented: ABC News, reporting on 14 February 2006 that a set of Saddam Hussein recordings would be released there, described “a nongovernmental meeting — called Intelligence Summit 2006 — this weekend in Arlington, Va.”, which puts the conference on the weekend of 17–19 February. What is not documented anywhere outside his own paperwork is that he was on the programme. His English-language résumé dates the same talk to 19 February 2007 in Washington D.C. — one more reminder that a curriculum vitae cannot settle a question about itself.

events.title: “Towards a diagnosis of the Latin American political situation”, at the America's Future Foundation
events.text: The last of the three United States talks his curriculum vitae dates, and the one his two self-written curricula agree on: both place it at the America's Future Foundation in Washington D.C. on 12 September 2006. With the Atlas talk of September 2005 and the Intelligence Summit paper of February 2006 it marks the other half of the emigration — the Brazilian polemicist becoming a speaker to American audiences about Latin America — a few months before True Outspeak began broadcasting. Nothing beyond his own documents attests any of the three.

events.title: Begins the online radio program True Outspeak
events.text: First episode aired 4 December 2006 — preserved with the show's own audio and a transcript ('estamos inaugurando o nosso programa') in an Internet Archive collection; Calil (2021) confirms the program. It ran on BlogTalkRadio until 2013 per English Wikipedia.

events.dateNote: The year is placed by what the account describes — the Jornal do Brasil column and the weekly web radio programme with listener questions — not by any date given in it.
events.title: A student lives in the house, and describes the working week
events.text: Ítalo Marsili's account, told years later on a podcast: he arrived in his early twenties with a one-way ticket and no money, having gone bankrupt, and gave the wrong flight time — Carvalho went to the airport eight hours early, waited, went home, worked out the real arrival and came back for him. On the lot stood a large outbuilding holding the office and the library, shelved as literature, theology and philosophy. The household lived on roughly 200 dollars from the Jornal do Brasil column; Marsili says he barely ate and began smoking to fill the gap. The week had a shape: talk ran until seven in the morning and the house slept through the day; on Wednesdays Carvalho read that week's newspaper article aloud to everyone in the office and they argued about it; on Mondays Marsili sorted the listeners' questions into a file for the radio programme. Testimony, and one person's, given long after the fact — the working week it describes is corroborated by the broadcasts, the poverty is not corroborated anywhere else.

events.place: São Paulo, Brazil (taught from the United States)
events.title: Teaching Brazil by videoconference from the United States
events.text: His own telling on the True Outspeak broadcasts of April 2007: the Seminário de Filosofia he had been running in Brazil since at least 2002 was by then reaching São Paulo by videoconference from the United States, hosted at É Realizações, and he announced a session for the 18th of that month. In February 2007 he put the teaching in a longer line — courses 'for twenty years', which he said he was continuing by videoconference — and listeners wrote in as students. What changed after the 2005 emigration was therefore the delivery, not the teaching: the Curso Online de Filosofia of 2009 industrialized an operation that had already crossed the Atlantic. Recorded as self-testimony from machine-transcribed broadcasts, not as an institutional record.

events.title: His YouTube channel is created
events.text: The channel's own About page records 'Joined Jul 7, 2007' — a primary source that contradicts Portuguese Wikipedia's 2015 launch claim (2015 may reflect when regular use began, but no source supports it). The channel passed one million subscribers by his death.

events.dateNote: Announced across several broadcasts for 'the last two weeks of April' 2008; the exact days of that first course are not stated. The three later courses in the series carry full dates.
events.title: Residential courses in Virginia, with students flying in from Brazil
events.text: Alongside the online teaching he ran short in-person courses at his own house in Virginia, and his broadcasts announce four of them: political philosophy in the last two weeks of April 2008; method in philosophy, 29 September to 4 October 2008; an introduction to the work of Eric Voegelin, 27 April to 2 May 2009, which he describes as a repeat of the previous year's; and philosophy of science in the second half of May 2010. Enrolment ran through a single intermediary in Paraná reachable by telephone, and he presented the fee as payable in instalments and deliberately modest. The students were Brazilians travelling to the United States: in February 2009 he tells those signed up for the Voegelin course to get their visas as early as they can, warning that entry had become only slightly easier. The two operations were not separate for long — in May 2010 he says the last class of the philosophy-of-science course went out on the Saturday as a session of the online seminar. Self-testimony from machine-transcribed broadcasts, paraphrased; the dates are his announcements, not an institutional record, and no attendance figure is given.

events.title: seminariodefilosofia.org goes live — as an archive, not a course
events.text: He opens the site on air, in the middle of the broadcast, describing it as a division of his own site. What it is for is the back catalogue: for years people had been asking for recordings and handouts of his old courses, and he says the material runs to more than twenty years of classes — some filmed, some on audio, some transcribed into apostilas, most of them never corrected by him and therefore provisional. Subscribers pay a monthly fee, five or six items are added a month, and the previous month's material moves to an archive that stays downloadable on an undertaking not to redistribute. The live course would follow seven months later. Self-testimony from a machine-transcribed broadcast, paraphrased.

events.title: Founds the Inter-American Institute for Philosophy, Government, and Social Thought
events.text: Founded in late 2009 (its web domain was registered 10 December 2009 and it operated as a Virginia 501(c)(3), per IRS records); Olavo served as president. He announced its closure himself on 29 November 2018 ('Fechei o Interamerican...'), reported by the press days later.

events.title: First lecture of the Curso Online de Filosofia (COF)
events.text: The paid weekly online philosophy course he taught until his death — 585 lectures over thirteen years. A student index and English Wikipedia date the first class to 14 March 2009. He announced it on 9 March as a five-year course beginning the following Saturday at three in the afternoon, Brasília time, and had been calling it a five-year course on air since at least January; asked why not a Friday or Saturday evening, he said he would not take people's night out. The community transcription corpus of the course is public (see references); this project cites it by lecture number and date only. His own broadcasts bracket the launch closely: on 9 March 2009 he announced the first class for 'next Saturday, the 14th', and a week later reported that they had expected about a hundred people and more than four hundred arrived, collapsing the streaming provider and forcing the bandwidth to be widened. The start had slipped for five months — promised 'next month' in December 2008, then 'February, March at the latest' in January, then 'a week, ten days at most' in late February — and the delivered format was a members-only stream with an open Brazilian phone line rather than the Skype arrangement he had described in October 2008. It began fortnightly and was weekly by that August.

events.title: A Mente Revolucionária at 550 pages, and the reason it was slow
events.text: Asked on air how the book was coming, he answers that he has written 550 pages and is barely half way through the subject, because each part carries its own documentation problem. The constraint he gives is time, and the list is a snapshot of his week five months after the COF launched: he has the programme to make, the Seminário de Filosofia to look after and newspaper articles to write, leaving one or two days for the book — much slower than he had expected, and he adds that he no longer has the wind he once had, when a night's sitting produced seventy pages. Self-testimony from a machine-transcribed broadcast, paraphrased; the book had not appeared by his death.

events.title: Says he now holds a green card, ending the visa constraint
events.text: He mentions it first in passing while signing off — he has his green card now, and the country he left has been stolen from him. Three later broadcasts of 2010 fill it in: he was admitted as a resident alien of extraordinary ability, the category he says is given to great scientists; it took four years of work and a thousand pages of documents; and he uses it in arguing for the Arizona immigration law. This bears on the shape of the emigration: the constraint under which he left Brazil in 2005 has an end date, and it falls here. Self-testimony from machine-transcribed broadcasts, paraphrased and dated to them; no immigration record has been sought or seen.

events.title: Names Padre Paulo Ricardo as his personal confessor
events.text: In the lecture of 30 October 2010 he described Padre Paulo Ricardo de Azevedo as his personal confessor; a year earlier (28 November 2009) he had called him the only priest in Brazil he trusted, and in May 2010 he recounted the priest's recent visit to his Virginia home. Together with his stated practice of confession as late as 2020 and the sacraments received on his deathbed (reported by Silvio Grimaldo of Brasil Sem Medo), this documents in his own dated words his return to full Catholic practice during the US years. The origin of that return — accounts circulate of a c. 2006 visit — remains unverified and is told differently by sympathetic and hostile sources.

events.title: Announces the Dugin debate, six weeks before it opens
events.text: He tells his listeners that a group of his students in Bahia is organising an internet debate between him and Aleksandr Dugin, whom he describes as the author of the Eurasian strategy and a kind of guru to Putin — and as a man of extraordinary talent and great culture, intellectually worthy of every respect. The format is set before the date is: written, on a site built for the purpose, with the text reproduced on his own site, on Mídia Sem Máscara, on the Inter-American Institute's site and wherever Dugin chooses. The question is which forces are contending for world power and what part the United States plays in it. No date is fixed, but he has been told Dugin is already writing his first piece. Self-testimony, paraphrased; the debate opened on 4 March.

events.title: Written debate with Aleksandr Dugin begins
events.text: The Carvalho–Dugin debate on 'The USA and the New World Order' ran online from 4 March to 31 July 2011, when both published their conclusions; the host site was reportedly accessed by some 200,000 people from over thirty countries. Sedgwick (2021) reads it as a debate about global politics rather than doctrine: Dugin began it believing he was debating a fellow Brazilian Traditionalist and ended disappointed, while Carvalho showed no interest in common ground — 'the debate, then, was not really about Traditionalism at all'.

events.title: True Outspeak stops without a farewell
events.text: The last episode preserved in the archive's capture of the series ends the way every other one does — the time is up, until next week, thank you. There is no farewell in it or in the five before it, and an unexplained five-week gap sits just behind it, between 16 February and 23 March. English Wikipedia has the programme running until 2013; the capture of the public playlist holds 201 episodes and stops here. Recorded as a property of what survives, not as an end date: whether it continued elsewhere is not settled by the material this project holds.

events.title: The Dugin debate is published as Os EUA e a Nova Ordem Mundial
events.text: Portuguese edition of the debate (VIDE Editorial, trans. Giuliano Moraes); still sold by the official Seminário de Filosofia bookstore.

events.title: Publishes O Mínimo que Você Precisa Saber para Não Ser um Idiota
events.text: 193 press articles from 1997–2013, organized by Felipe Moura Brasil (Record). A best-seller: English Wikipedia cites c. 320,000 copies; Poder360 reports 400,000 combined with O Imbecil Coletivo by 2019 — the figures differ.

events.title: Students of the course hold the first European meeting of the seminar
events.text: A gathering of Brazilian students of the Curso Online de Filosofia living in or passing through Europe, with Carvalho joining from the United States. Asked about exile, the answer given was that the speaker had escaped the disintegration it caused Solzhenitsyn because he still had his family and an audience of thousands in his own language, and that the exile a philosopher actually needs is temporal rather than geographical — leaving your own epoch to see it with the eyes of another. The year comes from the recording's own title; no date is announced in it.
events.dateNote: Two things about this source, both of which limit it. The recording carries no speaker labels, and it is a group meeting that opens with a host introducing participants by name — so the answer above is attributed to the event rather than to Carvalho, who is its host and its likeliest author but cannot be established as the speaker from the transcript alone. And the transcription is the worst in the collection: Solzhenitsyn survives as 'lula só flores'. Pending a speaker-attributed pass over the audio (archive#62).

events.title: Mídia Sem Máscara goes offline
events.text: Per Calil (2021), the site operated 2002–2017.
events.dateNote: Calil gives 2002–2017. The site was still serving on 3 January and 4 September 2018, so his end date is early by at least a year; the shutdown falls between September 2018 and 2021. Both positions are recorded rather than reconciled.

events.title: The documentary O Jardim das Aflições premieres
events.text: Josias Teófilo's debut feature about Olavo's life and thought, named after the 1995 book, first screened at Virginia Commonwealth University with Olavo present. An October 2017 screening at UFPE was disrupted — an episode sympathetic outlets described as violent repression (attributed; that account's link is unverified). The film had a limited Brazilian theatrical release from 31 May–1 June 2017 (Brasília, Porto Alegre, Rio, São Paulo) per AdoroCinema's own dated news desk — which contradicts the '2015' label on AdoroCinema's film page.

events.title: Near-fatal pneumonia; surgery removes the congenital tracheal tumor
events.text: In March 2018 a pneumonia he said 'nearly killed him' put him in hospital for about a month, and surgeons removed the congenital tracheal cyst the infection had inflamed (his own posts of 23–26 March, mirrored by the fan archive; reported by Boletim da Liberdade). His fullest account came in April 2021: born with a tracheal tumor that lay dormant until it broke the trachea at 71, an emergency operation at the VCU hospital with tumor removal and tracheal reconstruction, and recurring aftereffects that re-hospitalized him — two days in February 2020, again in early 2021. This is the 'old operation' of his c. 2020 lecture recollection, and the same congenital tumor he had described in a lecture of January 2010 — the point where his own telling, the lecture record and the press coverage all meet.

events.title: Bolsonaro's victory-night table displays O Mínimo
events.text: In his election-night livestream, Jair Bolsonaro kept on the table a Bible, the Constitution, a Churchill biography and O Mínimo que Você Precisa Saber para Não Ser um Idiota — widely read by the press as signaling Olavo's status as intellectual reference of the incoming government (that reading is the press's).

events.title: Ernesto Araújo named foreign minister; the press attributes the choice to Olavo
events.text: Fox News (14 November 2018) and other outlets reported Bolsonaro chose the little-known diplomat after Olavo recommended him. Attribution of ministerial picks to Olavo — Araújo at Itamaraty, Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez and later Abraham Weintraub at Education — is a press and academic characterization (Calil 2021; Gazeta do Povo calls him the ministers' 'guru'), which Olavo himself alternately embraced and dismissed.

events.title: The Bolsonaro government takes office with ministers labeled 'olavistas'
events.text: Academics and commentators (Calil 2021; Castro Rocha 2021) describe the Education and Foreign Affairs ministries as staffed on Olavo's recommendation; the press routinely labeled him the government's 'guru' or 'ideologue' — a title he publicly rejected, and which the scholar Mark Sedgwick also considers overstated. Sedgwick (2021), citing an Estado de S. Paulo interview of 24 November 2018, records the specifics: Carvalho was offered the education ministry and refused it, recommending instead his long-time friend Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez, and recommended the career diplomat Ernesto Araújo — who shared his interest in Traditionalism — for foreign minister.

events.title: Awarded the Grã-Cruz of the Ordem de Rio Branco
events.text: Decree published in an extra edition of the Diário Oficial da União on 30 April 2019, giving him the order's highest rank alongside state authorities; Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro received the lower Grande Oficial rank in the same decree. A bill in the Chamber of Deputies later sought to annul the concession as contrary to the order's rules — the award remained contested.

events.title: Launch of the online newspaper Brasil Sem Medo
events.text: Announced on 6 December 2019 and live from 19 December 2019, with Olavo as figurehead — reported independently by Metrópoles and Gazeta do Povo; the site is in the Wayback record by 26 December 2019.
events.dateNote: The 19 December date is the launch announced on 6 December, not an attested go-live. Three newsrooms reported the plan independently that day — Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo and Poder360, none carrying an agency credit — and all three state the 19th prospectively. The domain was registered 25 November 2019 and something was serving on it by 6 December, which a snapshot cannot distinguish from a teaser. What is firmly attested is the announcement.

events.title: Court upholds R$ 2.9 million owed to Caetano Veloso
events.text: Consultor Jurídico reported that his appeal failed against accumulated daily fines plus R$ 65,000 in moral damages, for refusing to delete 2017 social-media posts about the musician Caetano Veloso that the courts had found defamatory. In 2024 CartaCapital reported his heirs were notified of the debt.

events.title: Returns to Brazil for treatment: the InCor months
events.text: After the incomplete US bladder operation of May 2021 — two tumors removed, a second surgery needed, by his own account — he flew to Brazil in early July. His only stated reason: 'Brazilian medicine is better than American' (post of 9 July). Taken ill on the flight, he entered InCor (Hospital das Clínicas, USP) on 8 July with cardiac ischemia per the hospital bulletin, and on 13 July underwent a three-hour emergency surgery for urethral obstruction, revising the May operation (the bulletin gives 13 July; some later summaries say 15 July). Discharged on the 18th, he was readmitted on 9 August: the press reported urinary infection, sepsis, ICU and intermittent hemodialysis, while a family statement of 19 August denied infection and ICU — a documented contradiction between entourage messaging and the hospital record that prefigures the January cause-of-death dispute. He remained hospitalized in São Paulo into late October ('fearsome diseases subjected me to a complex succession of surgeries', post of 26 October).

events.title: Returns to the United States after treatment in Brazil
events.text: Returned to the US on 17 November 2021, after four months hospitalized in São Paulo (Folha PE; Poder360's obituary timeline).

events.title: The rift with the government, in his own dated words
events.text: It began, in his own telling, the day Sérgio Moro left the government: if he really were the government's guru, 'none of this would have happened' — Bolsonaro had never asked his advice (24 April 2020, reported the same day by Correio Braziliense). Through 2020–21 his target was the military wing: the public attack on Gen. Ramos in the Weintraub crisis (May–June 2020), and 'it is obvious the generals never supported the president' in defense of chancellor Ernesto Araújo four days before Araújo fell (March 2021) — every characterization his own. In December 2021, weeks before his death, he called Bolsonaro's re-election bid a lost fight in live remarks (20 December) and said he would vote for Bolsonaro only 'for lack of alternatives' (28 December). Metrópoles' posthumous report that he 'died resentful' of the Bolsonaro family caps the same arc.

events.title: COVID-19 diagnosis announced; course classes suspended
events.text: A message on his Telegram channel dated 15 January 2022 announced the diagnosis and the cancellation of his course classes. Some international outlets date the announcement to 16 January — a minor discrepancy the sources leave open.

events.title: Dies in hospital, aged 74
events.text: The family's statement, posted to his social accounts in the early hours of 25 January, said he died 'na noite de 24 de janeiro' and gave no cause; no official cause of death was ever released. The cause was publicly disputed: his daughter Heloísa — publicly estranged from her father for years — said he 'died of Covid'; his personal physician, Ahmed Youssif El Tassa, stated the death resulted from acute respiratory failure caused by pulmonary emphysema, a chronic condition, associated with congestive heart failure, bacterial pneumonia from methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and generalized infection, and was 'not related to COVID'; critical outlets noted the COVID diagnosis announced days earlier and his public minimization of the pandemic. His own lectures had recounted a lifelong pulmonary history — bedridden through his first seven years and, in a c. 2020 lecture, decades of asymptomatic emphysema after an old lung operation (per the community transcriptions). Each position is its author's; this site does not adjudicate between them.

events.title: Bolsonaro decrees one day of official national mourning
events.text: The decree of 25 January 2022 declared official mourning throughout Brazil 'as a sign of grief for the death of Professor Olavo Luiz Pimentel de Carvalho'; Bolsonaro called him 'one of the greatest thinkers in the history of our country'. It was only the second mourning decree of his term.

events.title: Burial at St. Joseph's Cemetery, Petersburg, Virginia
events.text: Buried on 26 January 2022 at St. Joseph's Cemetery, Petersburg, Virginia, after a closed-casket wake; the graveside service was conducted by Father Gino Rossi, pastor of St Joseph Catholic Church in Petersburg. Reported from the cemetery the same day by Mariana Sanches for BBC News Brasil, and prospectively by Folha de S. Paulo, which had the hour from the funeral home. The two accounts give 16h and 15h and are read here as sequence — the wake at three, the interment at four — rather than as a conflict.

events.title: Posthumous honors: the Biblioteca Nacional medal, then Curitiba
events.text: In July 2022 the Biblioteca Nacional's Medalha — Ordem do Mérito do Livro honored him posthumously, his widow Roxane receiving it (the family-side archive shows her at the ceremony on 2 July). That year's honors list was itself contested: writers publicly refused their medals over other honorees in the same batch, and the critical coverage that confirms his homage folded his death back into the cause dispute in the same sentence. On 25 April 2023 the Curitiba city council held a posthumous tribute session and moved a grant of honorary citizenship.

events.title: Heirs notified over the Caetano Veloso judgment debt
events.text: In early September 2023 the courts notified his heirs of the R$ 2.9 million owed to Caetano Veloso — reported by NSC Total (5 September) and Bahia Notícias (6 September); the CartaCapital article is in the Wayback record on 5 September 2023. The dataset previously carried this as 2024, an error introduced by a later related report.

events.title: Childhood illness — his own account
events.text: His most repeated origin story in the course: sick from birth and bedridden through his first seven years with constant fever, then suddenly and inexplicably cured around age seven, going straight to school afterward (told, among other places, in the lectures of 9 October 2010 and 20 April 2013). In a lecture of 16 January 2010 he added that he was born with an undiagnosed tracheal tumor still with him in his sixties; in a lecture of c. 2020 he tied his late-diagnosed emphysema to a lung operation decades earlier. All of this is his own retrospective testimony via the community transcriptions, unverified against audio — recorded here as testimony, not as a medical record. A second line of his own testimony describes the condition itself, twice. On 10 August 2009 he said he had been born with a tracheal tumour and an infectious bronchitis that was near-fatal for seven years — though a fortnight later he said instead that nobody had known what he had, a wobble worth recording rather than smoothing. Again on his programme of 14 April 2010 — eight years before the surgery and twelve before his death — he said he had been born with a tracheal tumour, which he sized by comparison to an orange. In the same passage he said he had smoked since fifteen, three packs a day for over forty years. Both are his own statements in machine-transcribed broadcasts and neither is a medical record; the first is the earliest first-person account yet found of the congenital condition that the 2018 surgery would remove, and it long predates the disputes that followed his death.

figures.name: Roxane Andrade de Souza
figures.role: Widow; received his posthumous Biblioteca Nacional medal (July 2022). When their union began is contested and this project does not resolve it: the English Wikipedia infobox gives a 1986 marriage, citing Benjamin Teitelbaum's War for Eternity, while the 2024 reporting on the estate describes a união estável of 'quase 20 anos', which places its start around 2004–2005. Nineteen years separate the two, and no source consulted here reconciles them. The Teitelbaum passage has not been read by anyone working on this dataset, so what that book actually says — and whether it attaches a year to this union at all — remains unchecked.

figures.name: Heloísa de Carvalho
figures.role: Eldest daughter, publicly estranged from her father for years and excluded from his will; stated after his death that he 'died of Covid', which his personal physician publicly denied. Found dead at her home in Atibaia, São Paulo, in January 2026; the cause was not disclosed

figures.name: Jair Bolsonaro
figures.role: President of Brazil 2019–2022; decreed national mourning at Olavo's death. The press called Olavo his 'guru' — a label Olavo rejected; Metrópoles reported (attributed) that he 'died resentful' of the Bolsonaro family after their public estrangement from 2020–2021

figures.name: Flávio & Eduardo Bolsonaro
figures.role: Presidential sons and public admirers; Calil dates the family's approach to Olavo to c. 2012–2013. Both received the Ordem de Rio Branco (Grande Oficial) in the same 2019 decree that gave Olavo the Grã-Cruz

figures.name: Ernesto Araújo
figures.role: Foreign minister 2019–2021; his appointment was widely attributed to Olavo's recommendation (Fox News, November 2018)

figures.name: Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez
figures.role: Education minister January–April 2019; appointment attributed by press and academics to Olavo's recommendation

figures.name: Abraham Weintraub
figures.role: Education minister 2019–2020; commonly described as an Olavo-endorsed pick (Gazeta do Povo calls Olavo the 'guru' of ministers Araújo and Weintraub)

figures.name: Aleksandr Dugin
figures.role: Russian ideologue; opponent in the 2011 written debate published as Os EUA e a Nova Ordem Mundial (2012)

figures.name: Frithjof Schuon
figures.role: Perennialist master; per Sedgwick, appointed Olavo his muqaddam for Brazil in Bloomington in 1986, before Olavo broke with him and became a fierce critic of perennialism

figures.name: Padre Paulo Ricardo de Azevedo Jr.
figures.role: Catholic priest (Cuiabá) and media figure; by Olavo's own dated account (lecture of 30 October 2010), his personal confessor — the best-documented figure of his return to full Catholic practice; the two later collaborated publicly

figures.name: Josias Teófilo
figures.role: Director of the documentary O Jardim das Aflições (2017), his debut feature

figures.name: Juan Alfredo César Muller
figures.role: Argentine psychiatrist and astrologer; Olavo's entry into astrology — asked him to edit a book in the late 1970s, and Olavo assisted his 1978 astrology course at PUC-SP (per Sedgwick 2021, corroborating the tertiary account)

figures.name: Stanislavs Ladusans
figures.role: Jesuit philosopher; Olavo studied three years at his Conjunto de Pesquisa Filosófica (Conpefil, PUC-Rio), leaving when Ladusans died in 1993 and the group closed

figures.name: Ahmed Youssif El Tassa
figures.role: Personal physician; publicly stated the death was from respiratory failure due to emphysema and associated conditions, 'not related to COVID'

figures.name: Felipe Moura Brasil
figures.role: Journalist; selected and organized the 193 articles of O Mínimo (2013)

figures.name: Caetano Veloso
figures.role: Musician; won cumulative fines and damages (R$ 2.9 million upheld in 2020) over 2017 posts the courts found defamatory

figures.name: Mark Sedgwick
figures.role: Historian of Traditionalism (Aarhus University); his 2021 Aries article is the fullest academic account of Olavo's Traditionalist and Maryamiyya years, and he coined the 'post-Traditionalist' characterization

figures.name: Gilberto Calil
figures.role: Historian (Unioeste); author of the key critical academic study of Olavo's trajectory (Argumentum, 2021) — critical perspective, labeled as such

figures.name: João Cezar de Castro Rocha
figures.role: Literary scholar (UERJ); analyzes Olavo's rhetoric as central to Bolsonarism in Guerra cultural e retórica do ódio (2021) — critical perspective, labeled as such

organizations.name: Seminário de Filosofia / Curso Online de Filosofia (COF)
organizations.relation: Two things under one banner, and the order matters: the Seminário de Filosofia is the in-person course, running in Brazil by 2002 and reaching São Paulo by videoconference from 2007; seminariodefilosofia.org opened in August 2008 to publish twenty years of back catalogue; the Curso Online de Filosofia is the weekly online course that began on 14 March 2009 and ran to 585 lectures. The community transcription corpus of the COF is public and is cited here by lecture number and date only. The Seminário's own founding date is not verified: the earliest origin claimed for it is his own, a Rio course of March 1987 – March 1989 that his CV says continued under the seminar's name (see the chronology, 1987).

organizations.name: Mídia Sem Máscara
organizations.relation: Founder (2002); his main ideological web platform. The .org domain was registered 24 July 2002 and the site was serving by that August, which matches the founding year given for it. Calil dates its going offline to 2017, taken down by a former collaborator, though the Wayback record still shows live captures into September 2018 — the end may mark activity rather than the site itself; kept flagged. It later returned on a different domain: midiasemmascara.net is live, presents itself as Mídia Sem Máscara and dates itself from August 2002, with material published as late as November 2024. The original .org now serves a parked page.

organizations.name: Inter-American Institute for Philosophy, Government, and Social Thought
organizations.relation: Founder and president; closed 2018 per English Wikipedia (single tertiary source for both dates)

organizations.name: Escola Júpiter de Astrologia
organizations.relation: Co-founder, in his professional-astrologer phase; about 140 students by 1980 per Calil

organizations.name: Maryamiyya (tariqa of Frithjof Schuon)
organizations.relation: Entered Islam under Martin Lings's guidance by mid-1985 and was appointed Schuon's muqaddam for Brazil in 1986 (Sedgwick 2021); Calil records a 1984 conversion and a short-lived tariqa of his own. Left 'within a few years' per Sedgwick — around 1987–88 per his own course tellings. All details are these scholars' accounts

organizations.name: Brazilian press (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Jornal da Tarde, Jornal do Brasil, Zero Hora, Época, Bravo!, Primeira Leitura, Diário do Comércio)
organizations.relation: Papers and magazines he wrote for from the 1970s to the 2010s. The Diário do Comércio column was his last regular outlet: a media-industry profile records it as 2006–2014, Calil says he kept it 'até 2016', and English Wikipedia's 'weekly column in 2019' is supported by nothing found; the precise period at each earlier outlet remains poorly documented

organizations.name: Gazeta do Povo & Revista Oeste
organizations.relation: Sympathetic outlets he wrote columns for late in life; both identified themselves as publishers of his columns in their obituaries

organizations.name: Brasil Sem Medo
organizations.relation: Online newspaper announced 6 December 2019 with Olavo as president of the editorial board, Paulo Briguet as editor-in-chief and Silvio Grimaldo as executive director; he called it the largest conservative newspaper on the Brazilian internet. Three newsrooms reported the announcement independently that day, none carrying an agency credit.

organizations.name: VIDE Editorial
organizations.relation: Publisher of the Dugin debate book (Os EUA e a Nova Ordem Mundial, 2012) and of reissues of his works

organizations.name: Editora Record
organizations.relation: Publisher of O Mínimo que Você Precisa Saber para Não Ser um Idiota (2013)

organizations.name: Partido Comunista Brasileiro (PCB)
organizations.relation: Brief youthful affiliation, c. 1966–1968, per Portuguese Wikipedia and Calil

disambiguation.note: Almost everything about this subject is contested terrain — his title, his influence, his death, and his own retellings of his trajectory. This section records the distinctions the sources themselves make.

items.title: olavodecarvalho.org is no longer his site
items.text: As of August 2026 the live domain returns a page of unrelated e-commerce spam (apparently lapsed and squatted). His actual site must be cited via Internet Archive snapshots (e.g. the 15 December 2021 capture). Do not link the live domain as an official site.

items.title: 'Philosopher' is a claimed and contested title
items.text: He styled himself a philosopher and taught philosophy for decades, but held no degree in the field (he left PUC-Rio's Conpefil without completing studies); mainstream obituaries write 'self-described philosopher', his students insist on the title without qualification. This site records who calls him what.

items.title: Two works named O Jardim das Aflições
items.text: The 1995 book (Diadorim) and the 2017 documentary about him (dir. Josias Teófilo) share the name; AdoroCinema additionally mislabels the film as 2015.

items.title: Not the other Carvalhos
items.text: Not the historian José Murilo de Carvalho (d. 2023), the poet Ronald de Carvalho, or the politician Salatiel Carvalho — search results routinely conflate them.

items.title: 'Guru of Bolsonaro' is an attributed label
items.text: The international press (NYT: 'Bolsonaro's Far-Right Guru') and much of the Brazilian press used the label; Olavo publicly rejected it, and the scholar Mark Sedgwick considers it overstated. It appears on this site only as someone's characterization, never in the site's own voice.

items.title: The COF corpus is cited, not reproduced
items.text: The Curso Online de Filosofia's community transcriptions (585 lectures) are public and of varying review quality, and the lecture header dates carry known defects. This project cites lectures by aula number and date only; the reception index in data/cof-reception.json records which lectures engage which philosopher.

items.title: The 2009 course is not where the teaching began
items.text: The Curso Online de Filosofia is routinely treated as the start of his teaching, and the two names are often used for one thing. The record separates them. He was teaching courses in Brazil for more than twenty years before 2008, by his own count; the Seminário de Filosofia was meeting in person in 2002, in the same room as the recorded history-of-philosophy course and on the following day; after the 2005 emigration it reached São Paulo by videoconference from the United States, and in April 2007 he announced a session for the 18th of that month. seminariodefilosofia.org opened in August 2008 to publish the back catalogue, and the COF's first class followed on 14 March 2009 after a five-month slip. In August 2009 he still lists the Seminário and the COF as separate calls on his week. So 2009 is when the teaching was industrialised, not when it started — and the Seminário's own founding date remains unverified.

_meta.selection: The twenty most engaged philosophers in the COF corpus by the corrected word-boundary measurement; shipped in two waves (olavo#2).
_meta.disciplineNote: Timeline entries assert the philosopher's own public record; the reception layer asserts what Olavo said and when — never what the philosopher 'really' meant (AGENTS.md rule 6). Scholarly date estimates carry approx: true and render with a flag.
_meta.readings: Qualitative reception (olavo#11 wave 2), drawn from the Curso História Essencial da Filosofia — eight recorded sessions of 2002, seven years before the Curso Online de Filosofia the counts above measure.
